text: What is the difference between val and var in Kotlin?
modelAnswer: val declares an immutable (read-only) reference that can only be assigned once. var declares a mutable variable that can be reassigned. Note that val means the reference is read-only, but internal properties of a mutable object can still change.

text: Explain what a data class is in Kotlin and when you would use one.
modelAnswer: A data class is designed primarily to hold data. The Kotlin compiler automatically generates equals(), hashCode(), toString(), copy(), and componentN() functions based on the primary constructor parameters.

text: What is a sealed class in Kotlin and how is it different from an enum?
modelAnswer: A sealed class restricts class hierarchies where all direct subclasses are known at compile-time. Subclasses can have multiple instances and state, whereas enum entries are singletons.
